paragraphs.source_en: Those were bad times for computer manufacturers. In May 1970, after years of unprofitable computer operations, General Electric threw in the sponge by selling the mess to Honeywell. After GE and RCA folded their computer lines, we came back with an article in the November 1971 issue of Industrial Marketing magazine. The article lit a fire under the positioning concept and generated many requests for reprints and more information. With two major computer manufacturers folding one right after another, the urge to say "I told you so" was irresistible. So later in the year 1971, we came back with "Positioning Revisited: Why Didn't GE and RCA Listen?" (The article appeared in the November 1971 issue of Industrial Marketing.)
